phases.brief:
OPERATOR RULING: loguru FULLY replaces output across src/ and is therefore a RUNTIME dependency, not a dev one. Gate banners (DECISION-NEEDED blocks) DO gain standard loguru formatting.

THE ONE CARVE-OUT — stdout-as-data stays raw print(). `scripts/run_ladder.sh` captures `python -m entropic_substrate.telemetry final-eval --metric nats_per_byte` via $( ) and feeds it to float(); a loguru timestamp prefix on that line crashes the ladder with ValueError. tests/test_telemetry.py::test_cli_final_eval_prints_only_the_number asserts the stdout is exactly '1.25'. Same class for scripts/run_exit_gate.py, whose stdout must remain a single parseable JSON object. Rule: machine-consumed stdout is DATA and stays raw; diagnostics and human-facing banners are LOGS and go through loguru.

TIMEZONE: use zoneinfo.ZoneInfo('America/New_York') via a custom format function, NOT a fixed EST offset — today is EDT (UTC-4) and a hardcoded EST would be an hour off for ~8 months a year. Pods run UTC, so this also renders pod logs in operator-local time. The structured JSON sink stays UTC ISO-8601 (human sink local, machine sink absolute).

THE PYTEST TRAP: loguru binds sys.stderr at HANDLER-CREATION time. pytest's capsys replaces sys.stderr per test, so a handler created at import time writes to the original stream and capsys silently sees nothing — the existing gate assertions would stop asserting anything real while still passing. Configure sinks LAZILY inside configure_logging() called at CLI entry, never at import, and add a conftest fixture that re-points a sink at the live sys.stderr per test.
phases.notes: Lands FIRST because it rewrites the output substrate; p2 then adds a consumer of the same events. Running them in the other order means p2's diff gets rewritten by p1.

phases.brief:
OPERATOR RULINGS (interview 2026-08-12), all binding:

1. TOPOLOGY: self-hosted MLflow server + R2 artifacts. Railway project = MLflow container service + Postgres service, R2 as artifact store.
2. SOURCE OF TRUTH: JSONL is the durable write substrate AND the sole gate input; MLflow is the read/query/citation surface. Backfill reconciles them so MLflow converges to complete.
3. GATE READ PATH: JSONL-ONLY. telemetry.py and run_ladder.sh are NOT to be touched — no MLflow client in the gate path, no completeness check, no dual-source logic. This is the ruling that dissolved the precedence inversion; do not reintroduce it.
4. FAILURE SEMANTICS: ABORT AT STARTUP if tracking is unreachable/misconfigured (catches bad URI, missing creds). After startup, LOUD-CONTINUE on blips: warn, count failed writes, record the gap in the JSONL, report loudly at run end. Never kill a 20k-step H100 run over a network blip; never silently lose metrics either.
5. KAPPA GRANULARITY: all 108 series (9 layers x 12 heads at full scale) as kappa/L{i}/h{j}, PLUS derived aggregates (per-layer spread, kappa/spread_max, mean|kappa|). Per-head trajectories ARE the E3 readout and head divergence is the E3'' trigger.
6. SEED STRUCTURE: nested, but PARENT-AT-AGGREGATION-TIME (advisor ruling). Seed runs write FLAT (params seed+exp, tag config_hash) — zero coordination, retry-safe, works across pods. A separate IDEMPOTENT `mlflow-aggregate` step queries children by config_hash, creates/updates the parent, adopts children via the mlflow.parentRunId tag, and writes mean/std/n_seeds. INVARIANT: a parent either carries the COMPLETE aggregate or does not exist — its absence is the loud signal. Naive parent-first nesting is forbidden: a run that dies after seed 2 would leave a parent carrying a stale mean, which is a false citable object and exactly what the 3-seed rule exists to prevent. VERIFY at implementation time whether setting mlflow.parentRunId on EXISTING runs nests them retroactively in the UI; if it does not, create the parent first but write NOTHING to it except tags until aggregation.
7. TINY RUNS: no MLflow run for --tiny by default; opt-in via flag/env. Mirrors the .dvcignore decision.
8. ARTIFACTS: DVC keeps every checkpoint (content-addressed to R2). MLflow additionally holds the final and best-by-nats/byte for one-click access. MLflow also logs the .dvc md5 + remote path, which kills the pod-local-pointer orphaning that run_ladder.sh currently warns about in DECISION-NEEDED #4.
9. R2 LAYOUT: same bucket, distinct prefix — s3://entropic-substrate-lm/mlflow/, disjoint from DVC's files/md5/. Reuses the EXISTING AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY (R2 S3-protocol creds already in .env). Endpoint https://62c7fd87a1874f1dee6b149ad40ac657.r2.cloudflarestorage.com via MLFLOW_S3_ENDPOINT_URL. NO new R2 provisioning is required.

LIVE TESTING (liveRequired: true): stand the stack up locally with podman — compose.yaml with the official MLflow image + Postgres, artifact root pointed at the REAL R2 prefix. `just container-test` builds/starts it and runs the integration-marked tests against it. Test against real R2, NOT MinIO: MLflow uses boto3, and recent AWS SDKs send integrity checksums (CRC32) that R2 has historically rejected — that incompatibility is invisible against MinIO and would only surface in production. If it bites, the fix is likely AWS_REQUEST_CHECKSUM_CALCULATION=when_required and/or AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=auto; VERIFY empirically, do not assume.

DEPENDENCY CLASS: mlflow is imported by src/, so it is a RUNTIME dependency.
phases.notes: Railway deploy follows this phase, not inside it: the Railway template (railway.com/deploy/mlflow) ships Caddy(auth) + MLflow + Postgres + MinIO; we deploy it MINUS MinIO with the artifact root repointed at R2. Caddy env AUTH_USERNAME/AUTH_PASSWORD gate the public URL that RunPod pods will reach; clients read MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI + MLFLOW_TRACKING_USERNAME/PASSWORD. The template's internal backend/artifact env wiring is NOT documented in its README — read the compose/config at deploy time rather than trusting assumed names.
